free_tier.stated: '$50 in free credits at signup, no credit card required. Concurrency is capped (see above) until you upgrade.' At the Universal-2 pre-recorded rate of USD 0.15 an hour, 50 / 0.15 = 333 hours of transcription. At Universal-3.5 Pro (USD 0.21 an hour) the same credit is 238 hours.

record.chaining: a free runner plus 333 hours of pre-recorded transcription is enough to transcribe a whole lecture or podcast archive once; pair it with a free object store from the storage lane for the audio, since the credit covers the API and nothing else. What breaks: the 5-stream streaming cap makes live capture useless, and a re-transcription after a model change spends the credit twice.

limits.value: the free tier caps streaming concurrency at '5 new streams per minute' against 100 for pay-as-you-go, so five live sessions a minute is the real wall on a free account, long before 50 dollars of credit is spent.

record.notes: These are inference credits, not general compute. The page is an llms.txt-shaped 'Authoritative Reference' block dated 'Last updated: 2026-09-28' on the vendor's own pricing URL, so it is the vendor speaking and the rung is documented. The page also warns that 'Defaults can differ between free-tier and paid accounts' and that streaming bills session duration rather than audio duration, which is where a free credit disappears without producing output. Expiry of the USD 50 is not stated on the page; a 12-month read would have to come from the console.

record.category: speech-to-text, text-to-speech and LLM gateway API, one-time signup credit

free_tier.stated: USD 50 in free credits at signup, no credit card required; one-time, not a monthly allowance. The credit is spent at the per-model rates: Universal-3.5 Pro pre-recorded USD 0.21 per hour, Universal-2 pre-recorded USD 0.15 per hour, Universal-3.6 Pro Realtime streaming USD 0.45 per hour, text-to-speech USD 15 per 1M characters. Free-tier streaming concurrency is 5 new streams per minute against 100 for pay-as-you-go.
free_tier.notes: models on the pricing page: speech-to-text universal-3-5-pro, universal-2, universal-3-6-pro (streaming), universal-streaming-english and universal-streaming-multilingual; text-to-speech AssemblyAI-TTS-1; an LLM gateway that lists OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Qwen models at per-token rates. unverified: whether the signup credit also pays for the LLM gateway and the text-to-speech endpoint, because the page states the credit once and names no product scope; unverified: whether the credit expires

record.interface_detail: REST at https://api.assemblyai.com (upload, transcript submit and poll); streaming over WebSocket at wss://streaming.assemblyai.com/v3/ws; Python and TypeScript SDKs
record.tooling: Python and TypeScript SDKs, and raw HTTP and WebSocket calls with the API key from the dashboard; every model id is set in the speech_models field of the request
record.chaining: the credit pays for batch transcription of recorded audio, which a free CI runner can post file by file; pair it with a free object store for the audio, since the credit covers the API and nothing else. The 5 new streams per minute cap makes live capture on the free tier a poor fit.
